changes: Corrected translation provenance in the document metadata. For 44 documents the metadata said the English had been translated by Google Cloud Translation; it was in fact translated by Qwen3.5 (University of Edinburgh ELM). Those rows now say so: Translation engine ‘LLM (elm)’, model Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, and a Provenance basis of ‘pipeline record’. A further 88 documents now record that some of their sentences were translated later by Qwen (for example ‘Google Cloud Translation, with 12 sentences by LLM (elm)’). The metadata file that ships with the program is the same file; the corrected one arrives with the data update.

Data update 2026.11.04.2: two documents repaired. Document 15 (Armenia, National Security Strategy 2007): 30 words had lost their apostrophe (‘Armenias’, ‘countrys’, ‘Russias’, ‘Azerbaijans’, ‘Irans’) because the source PDF has none; they are restored, and the 11 straight apostrophes already in the text are made typographic, so the document uses one form. Document 35 (Austria, Weissbuch 2012): bracketed German explanations that our processing had added to 45 entries of the abbreviations list, and that are not in the source, are removed from the German and the English text, and three terms left in German are translated (National Defence Academy, Gross domestic product, Federal Final Accounts). The search data, the document metadata and the viewer pages are refreshed; the program asks to download them the next time you start NSDDD.

Starting NSDDD with python3 launch.py --no-update now skips the check for new data as well as for a new version (it used to skip only the program update, so new data could still be installed over a search index you had rebuilt yourself). To keep a rebuilt index from being replaced at any start, create an empty file called no_data_update next to launch.py: new data is then announced but not installed, and python3 launch.py --update-only installs it when you choose.

New metadata file with provenance columns. The document metadata now ends with six columns describing where each document’s text comes from. ‘Text source’ is one of English original, Official English edition, English from bilingual document, Machine translation, Editor-supplied translation, or Unknown. ‘Translation engine’, ‘Translation model’ and ‘Cleanup model’ name the tools used, where they are known. ‘Processing date’ is the date of the record behind the row. ‘Provenance basis’ says what the row rests on: a pipeline record, a checklist record, the translation log, the editor’s statement of which model was in use at the time, or the metadata label only, in which case the row is an inference from the Language labels rather than a record. The first 25 columns are unchanged. The file arrives with the data update. The copy that ships with the program, which is used only when the downloaded one is missing, is the same file.

Data update 2026.11.04.1. Two documents were reprocessed. Document 835 (Lithuania, National Threat Assessment 2018): its text was cleaned and split into passages again (588 passages, where there were 623), so its passage boundaries and search results differ from before. Document 817 (Serbia, White Paper on Defence 2023): its English text was cleaned again (454 passages, where there were 564) and its links to the Serbian text were rebuilt. The search data and the document metadata are refreshed, and the program asks to download them the next time you start NSDDD.

Keyword and Boolean search now match exact words in every script and treat a phrase as separate words: "cyber security" finds cyber-security and cyber/security but no longer cybersecurity, and a wildcard (cyber*) stays inside one word. In the real index this halves the count for "cyber security" and removes some matches in Greek and Russian, where the old search also matched inflected forms (ασφάλειας for ασφάλεια). Searches saved before this change may not reproduce exactly.

New: a "Match inside words" tick-box (match_inside_words for the AI assistant and API) finds a word where it is part of a longer word, so Sicherheit also finds Sicherheitspolitik and a Greek or Russian stem finds its inflected forms. It is slower.

"Most recent document per country only" is now "Most recent year per country only": the metadata holds a year, not a date, so every document from a country's latest year is kept, and the result no longer depends on the order of the rows.

Corrected: "Hits per 1,000 words" in the normalisation sheet divided by the wrong number of words (the average length of the matched documents times the number of eligible documents), so it was wrong for countries whose documents differ greatly in length. It now divides by the total words of the eligible documents. Re-run any analysis that used this column.

The AI assistant and API now refuse document numbers they cannot read (instead of searching everything), accept a single country as text, and enforce the search page's limits. A data update that stops part-way records what it installed and fetches only the rest next time. The export's settings sheet records the NSDDD and data versions and the search date, and the Mean score note is corrected. verify_install.py warns if the index and the metadata disagree.
Metadata: document 560 (Moldova) has M49 code 498, and document 815 now says Slovenian rather than Slovene. The user guide is updated with the corrected hits-per-1,000-words example.
Corrected the M49 code of document 560 (Moldova) from 298 to 498; the metadata update arrives with the data update.

The user guide (PDF) is updated: current figures (default threshold 0.70, 1,394,688 segments, 39 original languages, 252 aligned documents, 186 documents added and 22 removed), more cautious wording on how reliable the score bands are, on machine translation (with a citation) and on document types, where Defence White Papers and Defence Documents are now described as differing.

Income group, democracy status and aid status are now taken for the year each document was published, instead of today's value. A Hungarian document of 2005 counts as Free and High or Upper-middle income as it was then; a document from before aid-status records begin (1996) has no aid status.

New: V-Dem democracy data (Varieties of Democracy, v16, CC BY-SA 4.0). Filter by the Regimes of the World category or by a range on any of 128 V-Dem measures, see the regime beside each result, and add the main V-Dem columns to the spreadsheet export (all 128 measures if you tick the box). The AI assistant and the HTTP API accept the same filters.

Freedom House history replaced with the corrected version, now covering every country with a rating (the United Arab Emirates, Cabo Verde, Uzbekistan, Kosovo, Mozambique and Tajikistan were missing or wrong) and the 2026 edition.

New: a document catalogue page, linked at the top of the search page, listing every document with its number, and a Document numbers box to search only the documents you choose (single numbers, lists, or ranges such as 100-110). The AI assistant and API take doc_numbers.
Added document 901, The Plan for a Stronger Canada (2026), in English and French. Corrected the parallel-text page of document 137, and rebuilt 750 and 765.

The default search threshold is now 0.70 (it was 0.72): in a check of 15 topics, passages scoring 0.70 to 0.72 were nearly as often relevant as those above 0.72, while relevance falls sharply below 0.70. It returns about three times as many results; raise the threshold for a tighter search. A search that finds nothing now says how close the nearest passage came and what threshold would find results.

Documents with an official English edition and an official German text now carry both: the German of 14 documents (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) is searchable beside the English, linked passage by passage. Greek for document 567, Slovene for 321 and 527, and Chinese for 479 and 70 are added the same way.

Search results now say how the English relates to the original: 'English (official translation)' when the English is the government's translation, 'English (official parallel)' when two official texts were issued together, 'English (translated)' for our own machine translation.
Document 643, a party paper rather than a government or parliament document, has been removed (834 documents from 125 countries).

The AI assistant (MCP) and the HTTP API now reload the search index by themselves after a data update, so German and other original-language passages are found without a restart. The search page still needs to be restarted.
Corrected web links and German source links in the document list.
The installer now checks every download against the checksum published with the data release, and deletes and re-downloads a damaged file instead of installing it.
Running the installer again after an interrupted or failed unpacking now carries on, instead of failing every time with a download error.

Boolean search: 'cyber AND NOT terrorism' now works even when the excluded word does not occur in the documents searched (it used to return nothing). A query that only excludes, such as 'NOT terrorism', or that uses NOT inside OR, now gives a clear message instead of wrong results.

The installer no longer offers to install into a Python environment in your home folder, stops with a clear message if installing the Python packages fails, and understands '~' in the install folder you type.
On a Mac, Launch.command and Update NSDDD.command no longer use the system Python, which on some Macs asked to install Apple's developer tools.
Only one NSDDD window installs an update at a time; a second window starts without updating.

Security: the Mac installer uses a fixed, checked version of the tool that fetches Python; on Windows, the Microsoft runtime is installed only if Windows confirms Microsoft's signature; the 'requests' and 'certifi' packages are updated.
CSV exports no longer let a spreadsheet treat passage text beginning with =, +, - or @ as a formula.
The README now matches what the installer does (disk space, Linux requirements, the Windows package, exports and search syntax).

The user guide PDF is now the 29-slide version: the slides on using an AI assistant to analyse results are combined into two, with clearer advice on what to give the AI (metadata, inclusion criteria, what to normalise) and what to check.

The user guide PDF is now the 30-slide version. New slides cover what is in and out of the dataset, reading results responsibly, and letting an AI assistant run searches or analyse results; figures are corrected (835 documents, 125 countries). The 'Getting NSDDD 4.0' slide now explains that the dataset itself will be archived on Edinburgh DataShare, with the original PDFs, plain-text versions and metadata files, and that the search tool is a separate program built on that data.

The search page now has a "Report a problem or suggest a feature" link under its title. It opens a short form in your browser with your app version, data version and operating system already filled in; nothing is sent until you press Submit.

The MCP server's Boolean search now warns an AI assistant when a query is very broad (more than 500 matching segments) and tells it how to narrow the search with AND terms, filters, a small result limit or an export. Restart your AI assistant after the update to pick up the new tool description.

The search page's keyword and Boolean help now explains how to search the original-language text: type words with their accents, capitals do not matter, combine languages with OR, and use semantic search to find the same idea across languages.

The MCP server (the link that lets an AI assistant use NSDDD) can now run Boolean searches: AND, OR, NOT, brackets, "exact phrases" and wildcards, with the same filters and export as keyword search. Restart your AI assistant after the update so it sees the new boolean_search tool. The optional HTTP API has the same search at /boolean.
The user guide PDF is now the 26-slide version, with a new Document Types slide and a redesigned slide on the metadata CSV (835 documents, 125 countries).

NSDDD now sends one anonymous count a day when it starts (app version, data version and operating system only; no searches, documents or personal details) so the project can see how many installs are in use. To switch it off, set NSDDD_NO_PING=1 or create an empty file called no_ping next to launch.py. The README explains what is sent.
The search page now has an "Open the user guide (PDF)" link under the title, and the start page links to the guide too.

The green update box now words its message correctly when a data update changes nothing on your computer (for example, if the new documents were already installed), instead of contradicting the release notes.

155 new documents from 2026 and earlier years, 835 in all from 125 countries. Seven countries are new: Cabo Verde, Kosovo, Mozambique, Niue, Tajikistan, the United Arab Emirates and Uzbekistan. 21 documents found to be duplicates or wrongly catalogued were removed. The new data arrives as a data update the next time you start NSDDD while online.
233 documents now have their original-language text aligned sentence by sentence to the English (it was 153). Six more original languages are searchable, including Serbian.
The search page header shows how many documents, countries and segments are loaded, so you can see which data you are running.
The "Add AI headings" button now sits above its explanation.
The NSDDD 4.0 topic-search guide (PDF) is updated with the new figures; the old v3.5 workshop guide is removed from the installer folder.
A data update can no longer leave the data half-replaced: if NSDDD is still running (or a file is in use) when an update arrives, the update stops and your existing data is left exactly as it was.
MCP: new optional setting NSDDD_LAZY_LOAD=1 lets AI assistants that give up on slow-starting servers connect at once; the search model then loads on the first search. Off by default.
The README now points to the NSDDD 4.0 topic-search guide, and the Windows package includes the guide in its app folder.
Added the NSDDD 4.0 topic-search guide (NSDDD_Topic_Search_guide_v4.0.pdf): search settings, keyword and Boolean search, clustering and using NSDDD with an AI assistant.
Every launcher now installs updates and new data by itself at start-up, including a copy cloned with git (provided you have not edited its files). Before, a git copy only announced them.
The green update box on the search page now lists what changed: the program changes, and any documents, countries or corrections added by a data update.
New documents and data corrections now arrive as data updates when you start NSDDD while online (only the files that changed are downloaded).
A program update that fails part-way now restores the old files instead of leaving a mixture.
Downloads work on a fresh Windows computer whose certificate store lacks GitHub's certificate.
Boolean search accepts quoted phrases such as 'African Union' AND 'peace', and bare words next to each other count as a phrase.
Program updates install automatically at start-up and tell you when they have.
The search model loads when the page opens, so the first search is as quick as later ones.
The search page explains that this is a pre-release version.
Windows set-up now downloads the data from the GitHub data release (the package is about 0.4 GB).
Fixes to links to documents and exports (403 errors), passages counted twice, and the Windows set-up checks.
